results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that confirms an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate carries a cryptographic integrity hash (SHA-256) so that any alteration to the record can be detected, and hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing its contents. 

Anyone can verify a certificate without an account using its QR code or by tapping an Attesté NFC tag attached to the artwork. The public verification view displays only the details chosen by the certificate holder, keeping private collection data secure. Unlimited certificates are included from the Collector tier up, while artists issue source certificates directly from their artist plans.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A Source Certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by the artist from their studio, confirming authorship at the point of origin. It captures the work's provenance from the very beginning—what we call First Witness—rather than reconstructing it years later from paper receipts.

It is different from traditional certificates because it comes straight from the maker's hand and carries a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash that is additionally anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps. This proves the record existed at that exact moment in time without publishing its contents, making it tamper-evident and independent of any single platform. When the artwork moves on—whether sold, gifted, or consigned—its record and provenance move with it.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is the very first commentary recorded on a new artwork at the moment of creation—the artist's own account of the piece, recorded in their own voice, SHA-256-sealed and Bitcoin-anchored as the origin every later record links back to. 

Recorded at the source and never backfillable, it is the strongest possible starting point a work can have. Every later link in the provenance chain builds on it, preserving the context, medium, intent, and story of making directly from the maker before the work ever leaves the studio.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
A physical NFC tag can be bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation. Once bound, you hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected, and the linked certificate's verification view opens automatically as a physical handshake between the artwork and its digital provenance.

If you are having trouble getting a tag to scan, make sure NFC is enabled on your device (always on for iPhone, or in Settings → Connected devices for Android), move the top edge of your phone slowly over the tag, remove thick cases, and avoid metal surfaces directly behind the tag. Please note that NFC tag scanning requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags. 

Galleries interested in getting tags can email galleries@atteste.art, and collectors and artists can reach out to info@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/troubleshooting

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across the app to help you identify, document, and explore art without replacing your own voice or judgment. 

For collectors, the AI can identify an artwork and its details from a quick photograph using the AI Art Scout, build a taste profile to give you personalised exhibition recommendations through the AI Sommelier, and guide you through multi-angle photos to draft condition assessments. You can also talk to the Atelier—a voice and camera companion that answers questions about style and technique in real time—or generate custom walking trails.

For galleries, the AI handles background busywork by drafting exhibition copy, press releases, artist bios, artwork descriptions, and follow-up messages, while computing a nightly Daily Pulse briefing and answering your questions through the Almanac assistant. For artists, the Curator AI helps draft catalogue copy from your photos and notes while keeping you in full editorial control.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/ai-features, https://atteste.art/features, https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-galleries, https://atteste.art/artists

You can also use the Atelier—Attesté's voice and vision companion—to point your camera at a work and talk about its brushwork, period, or provenance. results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account and data directly inside the app: open **Profile**, go to **Settings**, scroll to **Account**, and tap **Delete account**. Type **DELETE** in capitals to confirm, and your account will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account" and the team will complete your request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). 

Please note that deleting your account does not cancel an active App Store or Google Play subscription — you will need to cancel that separately in your store settings.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/account-and-data

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté offers a genuine free tier (Explorer, up to 25 artworks with no credit card required) and is built around AI-native features like Atelier, a voice-and-camera assistant that identifies artworks, drafts descriptions, and helps document condition. It features cryptographic SHA-256 provenance with NFC support and First Witness recording at creation, all inside a mobile-first app for iOS and Android priced at $19.99/month for unlimited collector use.

By contrast, Artwork Archive is web-only with no native mobile app, has no built-in AI assistant, and offers only a 14-day trial rather than a permanent free tier, with unlimited collector plans running around $36 to $42/month. However, Artwork Archive offers mature consignment management, public collection pages, embeddable profiles, and a Discovery marketplace with a Call for Entry board, backed by a 15-year track record since 2010.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative
